An exquisite hand-engraved imaginary atlas, a large panoramic literary map drawn on uncreased ivory cotton paper. Top-down cartography, not an aerial photograph. Extremely fine copperplate etching, delicate cross-hatching, beautifully observed natural geography, subtle muted moss green and warm grey watercolour washes, tiny restrained vermilion ink paths. A mature illustrated endpaper for an exceptional literary novel, quiet, mysterious, sophisticated.
A vast intricate world surrounds a generous open pale central plain. On the far left, finely hatched mountains and a dense woodland of hundreds of tiny individual trees, narrow valleys and winding rivers. On the right, an ancient walled city with intricate roofs, a broad winding estuary, small arch bridges, fields and cliff-lined coasts. Fine meandering paths branch at crossroads and lead to different settlements and distant unknown lands, suggesting stories and choices. Rich cartographic details near the edges, a few delicate contour lines fading through the spacious empty middle. The central forty percent of the image is mostly bare pale paper, reserved for overlaid website typography. Balanced wide composition with the lands framing the quiet centre, geography continuing beyond all four edges.
A flat high resolution scan, edge to edge artwork, almost white warm paper, restrained ink, subtle organic paper grain. No lettering, no words, no labels, no numbers, no border, no page edges, no book, no childish icons, no clipart, no cartoon, no thick outlines, no compass rose, no decorative frame, no distressed yellow parchment, no three dimensional rendering.
